sentences.text: Liaoningotitan was a medium-sized sauropod reaching about 10 meters in length with a shoulder height of 2 meters.
Its skull featured a convex ventral margin of the maxilla and a short, anteriorly positioned upper tooth row.
The lower jaw held nine reduced, un-imbricated teeth with asymmetric, elliptical-like crowns featuring lingual grooves, ridges, and a bulbous basal crown.
A redescription of the holotype — the specimen the species is based on — proposed that Liaoningotitan is affiliated with the family Euhelopodidae.
However, Zhou et al. (2018) classified Liaoningotitan as a somphospondylan titanosauriform that is more derived than Euhelopus.
This animal lived during the Barremian to Aptian stages, between 125.77 and 119.57 million years ago.
In a 2025 redescription, Bingqing Shan proposed that Liaoningotitan belongs to the Euhelopodidae family as the sister taxon to Yongjinglong.
